info.name: Veriqon QR Menu & Loyalty Platform API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the multi-tenant QR Menu & Loyalty backend: Super Admin, Restaurant Owner Dashboard, Public QR Menu & Ordering, Waiter Panel, and Customer Auth & Loyalty.

How to use:
1. Set `base_url` (collection variable) to your app URL, e.g. http://localhost:8000.
2. Run "Super Admin Login" (after seeding a super admin) or any login request — tokens and IDs are saved automatically into collection variables by each request's test script, so later requests in the same folder work without manual copy/paste.
3. Folders are ordered to tell a working story: Super Admin creates a restaurant -> Owner sets up the menu/tables/staff/loyalty -> Public customer views menu & orders -> Waiter manages the order -> Customer signs up & claims a loyalty offer.

Note: "Waiter - Live Order Stream (SSE)" is a long-lived Server-Sent-Events connection (polls every 2s, closes after ~55s). Postman will show it as a pending request rather than a normal JSON response; this is expected.

request.description: Generic login used by the original /api/me and /api/logout endpoints. Works for any role (super_admin, restaurant, waiter, user) — returns a flat {message, user, token} shape (no success/data envelope).
Seeded by database/seeders/SuperAdminSeeder.php (superadmin@gmail.com / 12345678).
All fields optional (sometimes): name, email, phone.

formdata.description: Laravel method-spoofing: file uploads must be multipart, which HTML/Postman cannot send as PUT directly.
Optional: update other fields in the same request.

request.description: Sent as POST + _method=PUT because file uploads require multipart/form-data. Pick an image in the 'avatar' field before sending. Replacing a photo deletes the old file; response includes avatar_url.
Creates the Restaurant record AND a Restaurant-owner user with a generated temporary password, then emails those credentials to the restaurant's email. name and email are required.

exec: console.log('Check storage/logs/laravel.log (or your mail driver) for the generated owner password.');

request.description: Flips active<->inactive. A disabled restaurant's owner/staff logins and public menu/ordering are blocked on their very next request. Response data includes the full restaurant (name, slug, email, phone, address, description, currency, logo_url, status, timestamps) plus the nested owner `user` object (id, name, email, phone, role, created_at).
Cascades: deletes the owner user account too, and (via DB foreign keys) categories, products, tables, orders, loyalty offers for this restaurant.

total_restaurants, active_restaurants, inactive_restaurants, total_orders, orders_today, pending_orders, active_subscriptions (right now), recent_restaurants (last 5, newest first), and monthly_active_subscriptions — an array of exactly 12 entries (oldest first, last entry is the current month), each {year, month, label (e.g. "Jan 2026"), count}. A subscription counts toward a month if its active date range overlapped that month at all, based on its own starts_at/ends_at/cancelled_at — so this is a true historical trend (e.g. a subscription cancelled last month still counts for the months before it was cancelled), not just today's snapshot repeated 12 times.

query.description: trial | active | expired | cancelled. Remove this param to see every subscription.
matches plan_name or the restaurant's name/slug

request.description: Pass ?status=active (as set here) to see exactly the restaurants currently on an active plan. Remove the status filter to list all subscription history.
restaurant_id, plan_name, and amount are required. starts_at defaults to now, status defaults to active, ends_at is optional (nullable = ongoing).
All fields optional (sometimes): plan_name, amount, status, starts_at, ends_at.
Sets status to cancelled and stamps cancelled_at — keeps the record for billing history. Prefer this over Delete for the normal business action.
Permanently removes the record — for correcting a mistake, not for normal cancellation (use Cancel Subscription for that).

Use the email/temporary password from the "Create Restaurant" step (check your mail log) — set owner_password manually the first time, or change it via Change Password below and update the collection variable.
All fields are optional (sometimes): name, email, phone.

request.description: Sent as POST + _method=PUT because file uploads require multipart/form-data. Pick a logo file in the 'logo' field before sending.
Read-only: the restaurant's current (most recent) subscription. Response includes remaining_days (null if ongoing, 0 once lapsed). 404 if the Super Admin has not created one yet.

Optional: update other fields in the same request.

request.description: Sent as POST + _method=PUT because file uploads require multipart/form-data. Pick an image in the 'avatar' field before sending. Replacing a photo deletes the old file; response includes avatar_url.

All-time + today snapshot: orders (total/today/pending/preparing/completed), revenue (total/today), menu size (categories/products/active/out_of_stock), table count, total QR scans, and the current subscription (with remaining_days).

Per-table scan count, order count, and conversion rate (orders/scans), plus restaurant-wide totals. A "scan" is recorded every time the public menu is loaded with that table's ?table= token — see "3. Public QR Menu & Ordering" > Get Public Menu.
The exact same data source and shape as Dashboard Stats, scoped to a date range. Omit from/to for an all-time report identical to the dashboard.
Read access to every order for this restaurant. Status changes happen on the Waiter Panel, not here.
Registered customers who have ordered from this restaurant, with their order count, total spend, and last order date for this restaurant specifically. Guest orders (no account) are not included.
name is required. description, sorting_order, status (active|inactive, defaults to active) are optional.

formdata.description: Optional. Enable and pick a file to upload a product image.

request.description: name and price are required. category_id, description, image, status (active|inactive|out_of_stock, defaults active) are optional. Sent as multipart since image upload is supported.
Sent as POST + _method=PUT for the same reason as the logo upload above.
status: active | inactive | out_of_stock. Reflected instantly on the public menu.
Returns qr_token and a qr_target_url (e.g. {app_url}/r/{slug}?table={qr_token}) — feed that URL into any QR-image library to print it. label must be unique per restaurant.
Invalidates the old printed QR code (e.g. a lost/compromised table card) and issues a new token.
Generates a temporary password and emails it to the new staff member (check your mail log).

exec: console.log('Check storage/logs/laravel.log (or your mail driver) for the generated staff password.');

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Buy 4 Pizzas Get 1 Free",
  "description": "Applies to any pizza",
  "product_id": {{product_id}},
  "buy_quantity": 4,
  "get_quantity": 1
}

request.description: title and buy_quantity are required. product_id is optional (omit/null to apply to any product) and, if given, must belong to this restaurant. get_quantity defaults to 1, is_active defaults to true.

query.description: The qr_token from the table's printed QR code. Passing a valid one records a scan for Owner > QR Scan Analytics. Omit it to view the menu without logging a scan.

request.description: No auth required. Returns only active categories with active (in-stock) products — out-of-stock/inactive items and a disabled restaurant both resolve to 404, never partially shown. Pass ?table={qr_token} to record a QR scan.

No account required. table_token comes from the table's printed QR code. Instantly becomes visible on the Waiter Panel's order stream. If you're logged in as a customer (send the customer_token as a Bearer header), the order is linked to that account AND advances their loyalty progress for any active offer matching an ordered product (or a restaurant-wide offer) — see '5. Customer Auth & Loyalty' > Active Offers for a Restaurant.
Looked up by the unguessable order_number (not the database id) so a guest can poll status without an account.
Accepts either a waiter's credentials or the restaurant owner's (the owner can act as staff too). Use the temporary password emailed when the staff account was created.
Load this once for the initial screen, then subscribe to the live stream below for updates.

Server-Sent Events: polls for new/updated orders every 2 seconds and streams them as `event: order` / `data: {...}`, closing after ~55s (a well-behaved SSE client reconnects automatically). Postman will show this request as pending/streaming rather than returning a normal JSON body — that is expected, not an error. Cancel the request manually when done testing.
Enforces the forward-only workflow: pending -> preparing -> served -> completed. Skipping a step (e.g. pending -> completed) is rejected with 422.
Closes the loyalty verification loop: confirms the customer's one-time code shown on their screen, scoped to this restaurant and rejecting codes already verified/rejected.

Creates the account and emails a 6-digit OTP (valid 15 minutes). Set customer_email to a unique address before running (e.g. casey+1@example.com) — the account cannot log in until verified. Check your mail log for the code.

token must be exactly 6 digits. Paste the OTP emailed after sign up into the customer_verification_token collection variable, or directly into this body. On success the OTP is deleted from the database (it cannot be reused).
Blocked with 403 until the account's email is verified.
Always returns success (win or lose) so this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate registered emails. Check your mail log for the reset code.
Paste the code emailed by Forgot Password into customer_reset_token first.
Full order history for this customer, across every restaurant they've ordered from (not scoped to one tenant).
404 if this order does not belong to the authenticated customer.

Shown directly in the QR menu. Requires a logged-in customer (but not necessarily verified) to view. Each offer includes this customer's own progress (e.g. 2 of 4 coffees bought) and is_redeemable (true once progress reaches buy_quantity) — progress builds automatically from Place Order, not from any separate action.

Requires a VERIFIED customer account (403 otherwise) AND enough purchase progress on this offer (422 with a "buy N more" message otherwise — see Active Offers for current progress). On success, progress is reduced by buy_quantity (any surplus carries forward) and a one-time redemption_code is generated — show it to staff, who confirm it via "4. Waiter Panel > Verify Loyalty Redemption".
